title: Every telemetry read takes SQLite's write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), so the company's readers and edge writers queue behind each other
label: bug
steps:
Read telemetry.connect(): it runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE before yielding, and every reader uses it:
- latest (351), first_ts (357), raw (363), series (451), heatmap (467), export_csv (587), latest_forecast (611)
- routes_telemetry._grid_signal (204) and routes_edge._seq_last (85)
Reproduce: while one request runs GET /telemetry?start=<now-400d>&res=1d (it aggregates about 576k rows under the lock), POST an edge batch for another site in the same company. The batch waits, up to busy_timeout 30 s.
expected: In WAL mode, readers use deferred or autocommit reads and run concurrently. Only writes (write_rows, next_seq, delete) take BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
actual: Every read holds the one write slot of the company's telemetry file for its fetch. Ticks (about 4 months of minutes per site), the fleet page (latest + first_ts per site, so 2N lock round trips), page polls and edge ingest all run one at a time. A CSV import's single executemany blocks all of them.
evidence: telemetry.py:101-112 (connect with BEGIN IMMEDIATE) and :82 (busy_timeout 30000). Scale: with 1 site this is unnoticeable. With 50 sites in one company file, every tick's reads, every 30-s /now poll and every edge minute-batch go through one lock at a time.

title: The telemetry series route lets any role request 400 days at 1-minute resolution, a multi-megabyte JSON answer built in Python
label: bug

expected: telemetry.series's own docstring says a request 'never returns more than about 3,000 points'. An explicit resolution should be capped or downgraded so that span/step stays within a few thousand buckets. Plan Part 11 asks for about 2,000 points.
actual: The route accepts any res with a span of up to 400 days (lines 27-31), and series() honours an explicit res (telemetry.py:438-440). The request builds about 576,000 buckets × 24 series as Python lists (tens of MB of JSON), runs for seconds and holds the telemetry write lock during the fetch. No permission is needed.
evidence: routes_telemetry.py:22-32 checks only t1 - t0 > 400*86400. telemetry.py:436-459 uses auto only when res == 'auto'.

title: The plans table grows about 13 MB a day per site with no retention; SELECT * readers pull those blobs; plan_messages has no index
label: bug
steps:
1) Each tick inserts a plan row with steps JSON (192 steps × 33 fields, about 132 KB measured on a representative step), the compiled slots and the summary. That is 96 ticks a day per active site.
2) grep shows no DELETE FROM plans, plan_messages or forecast_issues retention anywhere.
3) GET /control (polled every 15 s by control-page.tsx:48) runs COUNT(*) on plan_messages WHERE substr(sent_at,1,10)=?. Every edge pull inserts a full signed message there (plans.py:670-673), and the table has no index (store.py:169).
expected: Keep the summary and drop or compress the steps and slots of superseded plans after N days. Index plan_messages(site_id, sent_at) and acks(site_id, received_at). Select only the columns a reader needs.
actual:
Growth is about 4.5 GB per site-year in the workspace file, and backups.py keeps 14 daily copies of it.
Readers that load the blobs:
- plans.history (582-585) SELECT * loads 30 plans' steps for a list that drops them; plan-history.tsx polls every 5 min.
- fleet_row calls plans.current, a full 130 KB parse per site, on every 60-s AppShell fleet poll.
forecast_issues keeps hourly issues forever (telemetry.py:606-607).
evidence: plans.py:461-465 insert. store.py:168-169 (indexes). routes_plans.py:142. routes_edge.py:427. routes_sites.py:82-96. backups.py:26 KEEP = 14. Scale: 1 site is about 4.5 GB a year (plus 14 copies); 50 sites about 225 GB a year.

title: plans.active_at is called in loops (per genset run, per peak quarter, per outage); each call sorts all of a site's plans and parses a full plan
label: bug
steps:
Callers in loops:
- GET /api/sites/{farm}/genset (polled every 60 s, 14 days) calls plans.active_at once per run (routes_telemetry.py:323).
- alerts._peak_unconfirmed calls it once per past peak quarter on every tick for advisory sites (alerts.py:92).
- alerts.evaluate calls it once per outage (alerts.py:132).
Each call:
- runs _released_at, which reads up to 200 overrides;
- runs SELECT ... ORDER BY belief_time DESC LIMIT 200, which the (site_id, generated_at) index cannot serve, so it visits and sorts every plan row of the site;
- then runs SELECT * and json.loads on a 130 KB plan.
expected: Fetch the plans covering the range once per request. Add an index on (site_id, belief_time). Read only the step needed.
actual: Cost is O(runs × plans per site). After 14 days a site has about 1.3k plans; after a year about 35k. The farm's genset page (about 40 runs) then sorts 35k rows 40 times and parses 40 plans every minute per open tab, and ticks add up to 16 more calls per advisory site.
evidence: plans.py:603-622. store.py:168 has only plans_site(site_id, generated_at). routes_telemetry.py:321-325. alerts.py:91-95 and 131-133.

4) telemetry.import_csv decodes it again, builds a dict per row (DictReader) and a tuple per row (ingest), then executemany under one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then aggregate_day for each day touched.

title: Every tariff lookup first re-checks that the shipped library is seeded, costing an extra connection and a full key scan
label: bug
steps: resolve() (line 89), adders_for(), fuel_price(), fuel_prices() and versions() each call ensure_shipped(). It opens a connection and runs SELECT kind, key, effective_from FROM tariff_versions plus a fuel_prices check before the caller's own query. One vectors() or rebuild() resolves the tou calendar, schedule, tax, icp, prosumer and adders, so about 6-8 times.
